newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila cleric warns against hasty liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: Manila cleric warns against hasty liberalisation.

text.p: The Philippines' top clergyman warned the government on Monday against rushing headlong in pursuing the APEC goal of full trade liberalisation, saying it could spawn a "culture of hamburgers and coke".

Cardinal Jaime Sin said fears the APEC agenda of liberalising investment and trade would lead to bigger economies dominating the small and exploiting cheap labour in developing countries had prompted some people to reject it.
"It is imperative that the State not cede through over-hasty commitment to liberalisation...its duty to protect...our home-grown industries," the Manila Roman Catholic archbishop said in a statement.

"Indeed as a nation, even as world culture develops, it is imperative that we maintain...our multifaceted national culture, appreciating that world culture is not enriched by reducing all local cultures to one culture of hamburgers and coke."
Leaders of the 18 member economies of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum are to meet at Subic Bay next Monday to discuss how to speed up the liberalisation scheme.
Police on Monday arrested 21 students caught pasting anti-APEC posters on street walls and charged them with vandalism.
Leftist groups denounced the arrests as part of a government crackdown on anti-APEC dissent. Signs confiscated from the youths read "Junk APEC" and "Oppose imperialist domination".

The government has drawn fire from human rights groups for barring the entry of Nobel peace laureate Jose Ramos-Horta and arresting Filipino leftist leader Filemon Lagman in moves widely seen as part of security preparations for the summit.
President Fidel Ramos on Monday dismissed a local psychic's prediction that he would be the target of an assassination attempt, possibly during the APEC meeting.
"Thanks for telling me. Is that news?" Ramos laughed.

Earlier, the military said it was verifying intelligence reports that a Christian vigilante group in southern Mindanao island was plotting to kill Ramos for entering into a peace deal last month with Moslem separatist guerrillas.
